english: Where, grandfather, have we found honey? In the hollow of the old oak. Who guards the honey? Wild beasts guard it and bite. I am afraid of them. Don't tremble. We drive them away with smoke. Now you lick sweet honey. Is honey sweeter than milk? Taste it and you will know.
uncertain: widṓmes is 1pl perfect 'we know/found'; 2sg might be expected

english: What, grandfather, is sweet? Honey and mead are sweet. What is bitter? Unripe roots are bitter. Which of the two do you love? Honey, I love. Is anything sweeter than honey? A mother's song is sweeter than honey.

Mistress, guests are coming in the morning. What shall we cook for them? I will roast a lamb on the spit and prepare it in the big cauldron. Is there ale? There is much ale. How many are coming? Ten men and five women. Then two lambs on the spit.

Brother, the fire does not burn and the house is full of smoke. The wood is not dry. Who brought this wood? Grandfather brought it to us from the river. Bring dry wood and I will kindle the fire again. We brought it. Now the fire burns. Now set the pot on the fire.

Woman, I am thirsty. Give me water. Drink milk, it is warm. It is sweet. I am satisfied. Where are you going? I am going to the king's village. Take dry bread/grain with you. You are dear to me; may the gods give you good things.

I do not want the meat. Why, my child, don't you want it? It is bitter. It is not bitter; I put honey in it. Taste it. I tasted it. It is sweet. Give me another bite. Eat with ... now I will give you another.
